findings.message: Root composition is missing `data-composition-id`.
findings.fixHint: Add a stable `data-composition-id` to the entry composition wrapper.

findings.message: Root composition is missing `data-width` or `data-height`.
findings.fixHint: Set numeric `data-width` and `data-height` on the entry composition root.

findings.message: <audio id="ambient-score"> has src but no data-start. HyperFrames cannot own playback for untimed media, so preview and render behavior can diverge.
findings.fixHint: Add data-start="0" (or the intended start time) and data-duration if the clip should stop before the source ends.

findings.message: <div class="room-bg" data-start="0"> has no id, so Studio cannot use a stable edit target for its timeline and canvas controls.
findings.fixHint: Add a stable, human-readable id such as id="hero-title" or id="scene-1-card" to every timeline-visible element you want agents or Studio to edit.

findings.message: Root element has class="scene-container" and is styled by 1 rule(s) keyed off that class (e.g. .scene-container). At render, every sub-composition rule is scoped to [data-composition-id="scene1"] <selector>, so a selector whose leftmost part is the ROOT's own class becomes a descendant selector that cannot match the scoped element itself. Since #1886 the producer preserves the authored root as an inner wrapper, so this no longer renders the scene unstyled, but #root is the shape the scoper special-cases and the registry blocks model. Use it so preview, render, and Studio agree.
findings.fixHint: Give the root id="root" and style it with `#root { ... }` plus plain descendant selectors (`.kicker`, `#hero`). The runtime already scopes each sub-composition by data-composition-id, so a class namespace on the root is redundant.
